clue.text: Finish with lovely disguised shot on court

parts.note: to drop something is to finish with it, as in dropping a subject

indicators.note: the letters of lovely appear in disguise, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A tennis player ends a rally with a charming, deceptive stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis stroke played softly so the ball falls just over the net, an example of a shot on court.

clue.text: Cut diamonds upon diamonds

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed upon another comes first, so it reads above

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller cuts a heap of gems sitting on more gems.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'upon' puts D above ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut food into small cubes is the cooking sense, so the verb is a synonym of cut.

clue.text: Operating daily? Hypothetically

parts.note: a machine that is operating is switched on
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a newspaper might be running every day, in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true only in written plans, not in practice, is true in theory: an idiom for hypothetically.

clue.text: Girl declines to see African landmark

parts.note: Victoria is a girl's name
prices that decline are said to fall, so declines gives falls

explanation.surface: A girl turns down an invitation to visit a famous sight in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfall on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe is an example of an African landmark.

clue.text: Employ tool and eels set free

indicators.note: to employ letters is to put them to use in a new arrangement, so tool and eels are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler uses a tool and then releases the eels he caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employ' signals rearranging TOOL and EELS together.
explanation.definitionFit: To release or unleash something is the idiom, a synonym for set free.

clue.text: Slip lead off dog to fetch bird

indicators.note: slipping the lead off means removing the leading letter of the dog word

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: An owner unclips a dog's lead so it can retrieve a shot bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip lead off' removes the B at the front of BEAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Stone circle located by mate

indicators.note: one piece placed next to the other, side by side

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
pal is a synonym of mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A stone circle is found beside a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent gemstone is an example of a stone.

clue.text: Archbishop, affectedly proper, dined

parts.note: prim means stiffly and affectedly correct
to dine is to eat, so dined is ate

explanation.surface: A prissy archbishop had his dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief bishop of a province is given this title, so an archbishop is one.

clue.text: To run away with current partner is warranted

parts.note: to leg it is slang for running away
I is the symbol for electric current
a mate is a partner or spouse

explanation.surface: Eloping with one's present partner is justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lawful or justified can be called warranted, a synonym.

clue.text: Mimic shown in matter to be published about opening of theatre

parts.note: copy is text prepared for printing
ca is short for circa, meaning about

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An impressionist features in a newspaper story about a theatre's opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who imitates others is called this, a synonym for a mimic.

clue.text: Golf and water sport on the increase

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rowing is a sport on water

explanation.surface: Golf and rowing are both becoming more popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Increasing in size or amount is the sense, synonym of on the increase.

clue.text: One that office bungled, seemingly

indicators.note: something bungled is botched and jumbled, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone in the office apparently made a mess of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning judging by appearances, a synonym for seemingly.

clue.text: What one may do at a reception for model when breaking a finger

definitions.text: What one may do at a reception

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
to model for an artist is to pose

indicators.note: one piece breaks into another, splitting it apart

parts.note: a finger of spirits is a small measure, a tot
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: At a wedding reception a model breaks a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finger' looks like a body part but is a finger of spirits, a small measure of drink; 'breaking' sets the 'when' piece within the 'a finger' pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a glass and calling for a toast is what a guest at a wedding party often does.

clue.text: Tidy rapper adapted Beatles song

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A neat hip-hop artist covers a Beatles number.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1965 single by the Fab Four, an example of a Beatles song.

clue.text: Regrettably said of eccentric artist inside

indicators.note: the artist goes within the jumbled letters
eccentric means odd, so the letters of said and of are disordered

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Something sadly remarked about a quirky painter in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the two words before it into AFIDSO; RA, a Royal Academician, then goes 'inside' that.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase of apology meaning unfortunately so, a synonym for regrettably.

clue.text: Save me — deer rampaging

indicators.note: rampaging means running wild, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A cry for rescue from a charging deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone, or deliver from sin, is to save them: a synonym.

clue.text: Reportedly harassed an unpleasant woman

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: harassed means harried, and harried an is said like the answer

explanation.surface: It is said that someone pestered a disagreeable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bossy, bad-tempered old woman is the dictionary sense, so an unpleasant woman.

clue.text: Quarrel involving a restaurant's initial list of charges

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the quarrel word wraps round the others

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An argument arises over a restaurant's first price list.
explanation.definitionFit: A table of fixed fees or duties, which is a list of charges.

clue.text: All are mad about English beer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the E
mad means crazy, so the letters of all are go haywire

explanation.surface: Everyone is crazy about English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges ALL ARE into RALALE, and 'about' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Cask-conditioned traditional British beer, so an example of beer.

clue.text: First to commend a pamphlet about a medical condition affecting sight

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken
about means around, so the pamphlet word surrounds the second a

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet on a religious or political topic

explanation.surface: Someone praises a leaflet about an eye disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouding of the eye's lens causing blurred vision is a medical condition affecting sight.

clue.text: Risked being where many martyrs died?

definitions.meaning: something risked is in danger of being lost
martyrs were often burned tied to a post, so this is where they were

explanation.surface: Lives were endangered, as with the martyrs burned to death.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in jeopardy, and literally describes standing tied to a post for burning.

clue.text: Everything impartially considered, infers Allan is wrong

indicators.note: wrong means mistaken or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: To be fair, someone tells Allan his deduction is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to be fair, said when giving all sides their due.

clue.text: A Greek starter

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter A is spoken as this word
the first letter of the Greek alphabet starts it off

explanation.surface: A first course on a Greek menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a first course, but here it is the letter that begins an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the radio code word for the letter A and the opening letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A male cat, tiny thing

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat is described as a little thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest particle of an element, so something extremely tiny.

clue.text: Highlights dramas at college

parts.note: plays are dramas
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: The best bits of student drama productions.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a feature is to make it prominent: a synonym of highlights as a verb.

clue.text: Openly disobedient, fainted when disciplined

indicators.note: disciplined means knocked into a new shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rebellious person passed out when punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldly resisting authority is the sense, a synonym of openly disobedient.

clue.text: Cycling backwards, pick up flightless bird

indicators.note: the last letter cycles round from the back to the front

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: A cyclist going in reverse spots a bird that cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling backwards' moves the final R of HEAR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American running bird, an example of a flightless bird.

clue.text: Crew crossing island river must show standard

indicators.note: the crew word straddles the island letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
a stream is a small river

explanation.surface: Sailors crossing an island waterway must fly the flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional, normal or ordinary is the sense, a synonym of standard as an adjective.
